rule: After firing a coordinator's update timer with `async_fire_time_changed`, await `hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)` before asserting on refreshed state.
trigger: A test ticks the freezer by the coordinator UPDATE_INTERVAL, calls `async_fire_time_changed`, then asserts entity state after a plain `await hass.async_block_till_done()`.
rationale: The coordinator refresh is scheduled as a background task, so a plain block_till_done can return before it has run and the assertion sees stale state.

evidence.excerpt: ensure the scheduled coordinator refresh task has completed before asserting on updated state

rule: Run the translation generation script for the integration and re-capture entity snapshots after adding translation keys, so snapshotted entities show their translated names and object-id-derived entity_ids.
trigger: A snapshot .ambr adds entities with a `translation_key` set but `original_name: None`, no `object_id_base`, and generic entity_ids like `sensor.device_1_2`.
rationale: Entity naming comes from generated English translations; a snapshot captured before running `python3 -m script.translations develop --integration <domain>` bakes in the un-named entity ids that will not match reality.

evidence.excerpt: regenerate translations (`python3 -m script.translations develop --integration imou`) and re-capture the snapshot

rule: Do not snapshot volatile numeric sensor readings; snapshot the stable entity metadata (entity id, device class, unit, availability) and relax the fluctuating `state` value.
trigger: A dependency bump changes numeric `state` values inside a snapshot .ambr file, forcing snapshot churn.
rationale: Exact readings that are not contractual make the snapshot noisy every time an upstream library adjusts scaling or rounding.

evidence.excerpt: tests can become noisy and require frequent snapshot churn ... consider relaxing the assertions

rule: Snapshot the device registry entry once per test module, not once per entity.
trigger: A per-platform test loops over entity registry entries and snapshots the resolved `device_entry` inside the loop.
rationale: The device is the same object for every entity of the integration, so repeating the device snapshot in each platform test only bloats the .ambr files.

evidence.excerpt: we don't have to snapshot the device for every entity ... once is enough

rule: A regenerated snapshot must contain exactly one entity per unique_id for a config entry; prune stale blocks instead of committing duplicates.
trigger: A snapshot .ambr contains two entries sharing a unique_id under different entity_ids.
rationale: The entity registry cannot produce duplicate unique_ids in one run, so duplicates mean the snapshot is stale or an unintended duplicate entity is being created.

evidence.excerpt: entity registry should not produce duplicate unique_ids for one config entry/subentry

rule: A test must actually exercise the failure path named in its name and docstring; patch the dependency with a failing `side_effect` rather than a benign empty result that duplicates an existing test.
trigger: A config flow test named for a startup/discovery failure patches the discovery helper to return an empty result and asserts a generic abort reason.
rationale: Otherwise the new test is a rename of an existing no-devices-found case and the real error branch stays uncovered.

rule: Tests that enable a disabled-by-default entity must advance time to run the coordinator refresh and assert the entity's resolved value, not merely that the entity exists.
trigger: A test enables an entity via the entity registry and reloads, then only asserts `state is not None`.
rationale: Existence after reload does not prove the enable path works end to end; only a refreshed state proves the coordinator populates the entity.

evidence.excerpt: Consider advancing time/firing a time-changed event ... asserting the HDR sensor state resolves

rule: Obtain registries through the provided pytest fixtures (`entity_registry: er.EntityRegistry`, `device_registry`, `issue_registry`) declared as test/fixture parameters, not by calling `er.async_get(hass)` inside the body.
trigger: A test or conftest fixture body calls `er.async_get(hass)` / `dr.async_get(hass)` instead of taking the registry fixture.
rationale: The shared fixtures are the house pattern for registry access in Home Assistant tests and keep the dependency visible in the signature.

rule: Assert that entities were not created by querying the entity registry for the config entry (by unique_id or original_name) rather than by guessing generated entity_id slugs.
trigger: A test asserts `hass.states.get("<domain>.<guessed_slug>") is None`, especially for names containing characters that alter slugging (e.g. "2+", "2-way").
rationale: A mistyped slug makes the assertion vacuously pass even when the entity does exist under the real slug, so the negative test proves nothing.

evidence.excerpt: can silently pass even if the entity exists under a different slug

rule: Assert that a specific repair issue key is absent rather than that the whole issue registry is empty.
trigger: A test asserts `len(issue_registry.issues) == 0` or compares the full issue registry contents.
rationale: The issue registry is global and unrelated integrations can register issues in the same run, making the emptiness assertion brittle.

evidence.excerpt: brittle because unrelated tests/integrations can register issues in the same registry

rule: Deprecation repair issues must have test coverage for every branch that selects a different translation key, including the entity-used-in-automations/scripts variant and its placeholder substitution.
trigger: A repairs test only covers the plain deprecated-entity issue while the implementation also raises a `*_scripts`/`*_automations` variant with an `{items}` placeholder.
rationale: The alternate translation key and its placeholder are what the user actually sees when the entity is referenced elsewhere, and nothing else verifies the placeholder is populated.

evidence.excerpt: so the issue uses the *_scripts translation key and populates the {items} placeholder correctly

rule: When a change tightens validation, fix the existing tests it breaks instead of deleting them.
trigger: A diff that adds stricter validation also removes an existing test function.
rationale: Deleting the failing test silently drops the coverage the behaviour it asserted still needs; updating it (e.g. setting a valid `color_mode`) keeps that coverage.

evidence.excerpt: Prefer updating/restoring the test ... instead of deleting it, to avoid losing coverage

rule: When a service response model gains fields, add a test case where those fields carry non-default values rather than only the default None case.
trigger: A test's expected service-response dict gains new keys whose asserted values are all `None`.
rationale: Only the None path is exercised, so the code that maps real values (or NullValue) from the device response stays unverified.

evidence.excerpt: so the new response fields are verified beyond the default None case

rule: A test parametrized over a fixture-overriding value must declare that fixture as a function parameter.
trigger: `@pytest.mark.parametrize("mqtt_config_entry_data", ...)` (or another fixture-override parametrization) sits above a test whose signature omits that name.
rationale: Pytest fails collection with "function uses no argument" and the parametrization is silently not applied.

evidence.excerpt: otherwise pytest will fail collection with "function uses no argument 'mqtt_config_entry_data'"
so the parametrization is applied and pytest can collect the test

rule: Unique_id migration tests must round-trip every unique_id format the integration produces (device, multi-channel and group variants) and must not let one format's pattern match another's ids.
trigger: A migration test derives old-format unique_ids with string slicing/suffix matching and skips entries where the channel is None.
rationale: Skipped or loosely matched cases produce false positives, so the test stops detecting mismatches between the migration map and the runtime unique_ids.

evidence.excerpt: those cases are skipped or can yield false positives, reducing the test's ability to detect

rule: Conditions and triggers that filter their targets by supported domain need a negative test proving the condition does not pass when only unsupported entities are targeted.
trigger: A new condition/trigger test file covers only supported entity domains, including a `behavior='all'` case.
rationale: With `behavior='all'`, filtering away every unsupported entity leaves an empty set that evaluates vacuously true, so the positive tests hide the bug.

evidence.excerpt: behavior='all', which can otherwise become vacuously true if no supported entities

rule: Matter node fixtures must list any cluster whose attributes they define in that endpoint's Descriptor ServerList.
trigger: A `tests/components/matter/fixtures/nodes/*.json` adds attributes for a cluster id that is absent from the endpoint's `65531` server list.
rationale: A real node advertises its clusters in the descriptor, so a fixture that omits it makes discovery tests diverge from device behaviour.

evidence.excerpt: endpoint 1's server cluster list does not include that cluster
